title: Servepath Latency Cascade Inspector — model+route + streaming vs non-streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a single diagnostic dashboard ('Latency Cascade Inspector') that lets SREs and runtime owners quickly identify latency sources for a given model+route, comparing p50/p95/p99 across streaming vs non-streaming IO modes and request shapes.

Scope:
- Aggregate end-to-end request latency and a breakdown by serving components (proxy, router, runtime queue, kernel execution, KV cache miss penalty, network) for each model and route.
- Split views by IO mode: streaming vs non-streaming (blocking).
- Expose histograms and percentile trends (p50/p95/p99) plus an interactive waterfall for a selected percentile and time window.
- Surface correlated error rates and tail error signatures alongside latency slices.
- Provide trace links and quick filters for request_shape (prompt length, generation tokens), model_version, and customer tier.

Telemetry and instrumentation work needed:
- Tracing: add/standardize span tags: serve_path, route_id, model_family, model_version, io_mode (stream|sync), request_shape_bucket. Instrument middleware to attach KV cache hit/miss spans.
- Metrics: emit a Prometheus-friendly histogram for e2e_latency_ms + component_latencies_ms per model_route/io_mode. Ensure buckets cover 1ms..30s to capture tails.
- Logs: augment access logs with request_shape summary and model_version to correlate with high-latency traces.
- Pipeline: update metrics ingestion config (Cortex/M3) to accept the new histogram series and create pre-aggregated rollup for p50/p95/p99 to avoid expensive on-the-fly queries.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New dashboard with model+route selector, IO mode toggle, and percentile time series (p50/p95/p99) visible for last 1h/6h/24h.
2) Waterfall drilldown for selected percentile that highlights top contributing components and % contribution.
3) Trace links from waterfall entries open tracing UI with pre-applied filters.
4) Alerts: example SLO rule templates for p95 latency per-route (configurable).
5) Documentation (console doc + runbook) and one internal demo session recorded.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Auto-remediation or autoscaling policies based on this dashboard. (We'll follow up in a separate ticket.)

Design trade-offs / notes:
- We will pre-aggregate percentiles at ingestion to keep dashboard queries fast. Trade-off: introduces some staleness on >1m windows and additional ingestion storage.
- Component-level latencies will be emitted as separate series and normalized in the UI to compute contribution. This avoids adding heavy histograms for every internal subcomponent.
- Streaming mode telemetry differs (many small token events). For streaming, we will compute session-level end-to-end latency and token-emission latency separately; waterfall will emphasize session milestones (first token, last token).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Instrumentation sprint (2 days): add span tags, cache spans, and log fields.
2) Metrics pipeline changes (3 days): update ingestion config, add rollup job for percentiles.
3) Dashboard build (3 days): frontend panels, waterfall UI, trace linking.
4) QA + Demo (2 days): synthetic traffic + internal dogfood + demo.

Links and artifacts:
- PR (tracing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
- PR (metrics ingest): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-config/pull/63
- WIP dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood-internal/d/obs/latency-cascade-proto
- Runbook draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1LatRunbook
